metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: The induction. Okay. So-

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: But there's ways of getting computable approximations of the AXE model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So then it's at least computable. It is still way beyond any resources anybody will ever have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: But then the Gertl Machine could sort of improve it further and further in an exact way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So is it theoretically possible that the Gertl Machine process could improve? Isn't AXE already

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: optimal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: It is optimal in terms of the reward collected over its interaction cycles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but it takes infinite time to produce one action. And the world continues whether you want it or

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: not. So the model is assuming you had an oracle, which solved this problem and then in the next

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: 100 milliseconds or the reaction time you need gives the answer, then AXE is optimal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So it's optimal in sense of data, also from learning efficiency and data efficiency,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but not in terms of computation time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: And then the other Gertl Machine in theory, but probably not provably could make it go faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Okay. Interesting. Those two components are super interesting. The sort of the perfect

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: intelligence combined with self-improvement. Sort of proof of self-improvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So you're always getting the correct answer and you're improving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Beautiful ideas. Okay. So you've also mentioned that different kinds of things in the chase of

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: solving this reward, sort of optimizing for the goal, interesting human things could emerge. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: is there a place for consciousness within AXE?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Where does, maybe you can comment because I suppose we humans are just another instantiation

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: by AXE agents and we seem to have consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: You say humans are an instantiation of an AXE agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Oh, that would be amazing. But I think that's not true even for the smartest and most rational

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: humans. I think maybe we are very crude approximations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Interesting. I mean, I tend to believe again, I'm really, I'm not a very rational person,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but I tend to believe that our flaws are part of the optimal. So we tend to laugh off and criticize

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: our flaws and I tend to think that that's actually close to an optimal behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Well, some flaws, if you think more carefully about it, are actually not flaws. Yeah. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I think there are still enough flaws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I don't know. It's unclear. As a student of history, I think that's a very good point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yeah. As a student of history, I think all the suffering that we've endured as a civilization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: it's possible that that's the optimal amount of suffering we need to endure

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: to minimize long-term suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: That's your Russian background, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: That's the Russian. Whether we humans are or not instantiations of an AXE agent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: do you think there's a consciousness to something that could emerge in a computational form of

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: framework like AXE?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Let me also ask you a question. Do you think I'm conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yeah, that's a good question. That tie is confusing me, but I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: You think that makes me unconscious because it strangles me?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: If an agent were to solve the imitation game posed by Turing, I think that would be dressed

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: similarly to you because there's a flamboyant, interesting, complex behavior pattern that

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: sells that you're human and you're conscious. But why do you ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Was it a yes or was it a no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yes. I think you're conscious, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yeah. You explain somehow why, but you infer that from my behavior, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: You can never be sure about that. I think the same thing will happen with any intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: agent we develop if it behaves in a way sufficiently close to humans or maybe even not humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I mean, maybe a dog is also sometimes a little bit self-conscious, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: If it behaves in a way where we attribute typically consciousness, we would attribute

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: consciousness to these intelligent systems and AXE probably in particular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: That of course doesn't answer the question whether it's really conscious and that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: the big hard problem of consciousness. Maybe I'm a zombie. I mean, not the movie zombie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but the philosophical zombie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Is to you the display of consciousness close enough to consciousness from a perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: of AGI that the distinction of the hard problem of consciousness is not an interesting one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I think we don't have to worry about the consciousness problem, especially the hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: problem for developing AGI. I think we progress. At some point, we have solved all the technical

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: problems and this system will behave intelligent and then super intelligent and this consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: will emerge. I mean, definitely it will display behavior, which we will interpret as conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: And then it's a philosophical question, did this consciousness really emerge or is it

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: a zombie which just fakes everything?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: We still don't have to figure that out, although it may be interesting, at least from a philosophical

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: point of view, it's very interesting, but it may also be sort of practically interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: You know, there's some people say, if it's just faking consciousness and feelings, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: we don't need to be concerned about rights, but if it's real conscious and has feelings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: then we need to be concerned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I can't wait till the day where AI systems exhibit consciousness because it'll truly

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: be some of the hardest ethical questions of what we do with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: It is rather easy to build systems which people ascribe consciousness. And I give you an analogy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I mean, remember, maybe it was before you were born, the Tamagotchi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yeah, before you were born. How dare you, sir.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Why? That's the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yeah, but I...

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Because you're young, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yes, it's good. Thank you. Thank you very much. But I was also in the Soviet Union. We didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: have any of those fun things. But you have heard about this Tamagotchi, which was really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: really primitive actually for the time it was. And you could raise this and kids got so attached

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: to it and didn't want to let it die. And I would have probably, if we would have asked

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: the children, do you think this Tamagotchi is conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: They would have said yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Yes, I would guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I think that's kind of a beautiful thing, actually, because that consciousness is very

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: important. Because ascribing consciousness seems to create a deeper connection, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: is a powerful thing. But we have to be careful on the ethics side of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Well, let me ask about the AGI community broadly. You kind of represent some of the most serious

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: work on AGI, at least earlier. And DeepMind represents serious work on AGI these days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: But why in your sense is the AGI community so small or has been so small until maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: DeepMind came along? Why aren't more people seriously working on human level and superhuman

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: level intelligence from a formal perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Okay, from a formal perspective, that's sort of an extra point. So I think there are a couple

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: of reasons. AI came in waves, AI winters and AI summers, and then there were big promises

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: which were not fulfilled. And people got disappointed. But narrow AI solving particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: problems, which seemed to require intelligence, was always to some extent successful. And there

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: were improvements, small steps. And if you build something which is useful for society,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: or industrial useful, then there's a lot of funding. So I guess it was in parts the money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: which drives people to develop specific systems solving specific tasks. But you would think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: at least in university, you should be able to do ivory tower research. And that was probably

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: better a long time ago, but even nowadays, there's quite some pressure of doing applied research or

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: translational research. And it's harder to get grants as a theorist. So that also drives people

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: away. It's maybe also harder attacking the general intelligence problem. So I think enough people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I mean, maybe a small number were still interested in formalizing intelligence and

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: thinking of general intelligence. But not much came up, right? Or not much great stuff came up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So what do you think we talked about the formal big light at the end of the tunnel,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but from the engineering perspective, what do you think it takes to build an AGI system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Is that and I don't know if that's a stupid question, or a distinct question from everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: we've been talking about IAXE. But what do you see as the steps that are necessary to take to

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: start to try to build something? So you want to blueprint now and then you go off and do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: That's the whole point of this conversation. I'm trying to squeeze that in there. Now, is there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I mean, what's your intuition? Is it in the robotics space or something that has a body

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: and tries to explore the world? Is it in the reinforcement learning space, like the efforts

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: with AlphaZero and AlphaStar that are kind of exploring how you can solve it through in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: simulation in the gaming world? Is there stuff in sort of all the transformer work in natural

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: English processing, sort of maybe attacking the open domain dialogue? Like what, where do you see

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: a promising pathways? Let me pick the embodiment maybe. So embodiment is important, yes and no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: I don't believe that we need a physical robot walking or rolling around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: interacting with the real world in order to achieve AGI. And I think it's more of a distraction

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: probably than helpful. It's sort of confusing the body with the mind. For industrial applications or

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: near term applications, of course we need robots for all kinds of things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: but for solving the big problem, at least at this stage, I think it's not necessary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: But the answer is also yes, that I think the most promising approach is that you have an agent

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: and that can be a virtual agent in a computer interacting with an environment, possibly a 3D

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: simulated environment like in many computer games. And you train and learn the agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: Even if you don't intend to later put it sort of this algorithm in a robot brain and leave it forever

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: in the virtual reality, getting experience in a, although it's just simulated 3D world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: is possibly, and I say possibly important to understand things on a similar level as humans do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: especially if the agent or primarily if the agent wants needs to interact with the humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: If you talk about objects on top of each other in space and flying in cars and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: and the agent has no experience with even virtual 3D worlds, it's probably hard to grasp.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: So if you develop an abstract agent, say we take the mathematical path and we just want to build

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: an agent which can prove theorems and becomes a better and better mathematician, then this agent

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: needs to be able to reason in very abstract spaces and then maybe sort of putting it into

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: 3D environments, simulated is even harmful. It should sort of, you put it in, I don't know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: an environment which it creates itself or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: It seems like you have an interesting, rich, complex trajectory through life in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #75

body.input: your journey of ideas. So it's interesting to ask what books, technical fiction, philosophical

body.input: We all live in a certain context. We're all living in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Our own personal histories matter a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And also the larger context and environment in which we're living in and where we live and who we live with and, you know, the kinds of lives that we lead as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Those are all extraordinarily important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I mean, I know that from myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Everything that I've done in my life has been shaped by where I came from, who I was, my family and the way that we looked at things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You can't take yourself out of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I mean, you can do it in some, you know, like a science or something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But, you know, still your own views and maybe some of the ideas that you have in pursuing an experiment might have been shaped by your larger context, you know, depending on what it is that you work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But the other thing is the nature of the political system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: The presidential election is like a personality contest, a beauty contest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It's like a kind of a referendum on, you know, one person or another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It's kind of like what we see in Russia, honestly, with, you know, Putin or not Putin or Putin and Putin before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You know, it's all about Putin. And, you know, what do you think about Putin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It's not about what the president should be doing and, you know, kind of what their policies are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: That's kind of the bizarreness of the U.S. political system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Look, we've just seen this happening in the United Kingdom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You've got this core of a couple of thousand, couple of hundred thousand, rather, people in the conservative party have just voted for, you know, three leaders in a row.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: The rest of the country isn't. And they're just looking at, you know, whether they like that personality and, you know, what they say to them rather than what they're necessarily going to do for the country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I mean, which is, you know, kind of pretty absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And again, the presidency is a weird hybrid in the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You know, we were talking before about the person should be running the country, the chief executive or the prime minister in another setting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But we don't think of it like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: So, you know, we'd like to hang out with him or that, you know, one of my younger relatives and I said, so why did you vote for Trump?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Oh, I couldn't go vote for them because of this, or I couldn't vote for them because of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: What do you think about Vladimir Putin, the man and the leader?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Well, if you looked at the first couple of terms. Of his presidency, I think, you know, on the overall ledger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you would have actually said that he made a lot of achievements from Russia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Now, there was, of course, the pretty black period of the war in Chechnya, but, you know, he didn't start that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: That was Boris Yeltsin. That was obviously a pretty catastrophic event.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But if you look at then other parts of the ledger of what Putin was doing, you know, from the 2000s, you know, onwards,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: he stabilized the Russian economy, brought back, you know, kind of confidence in the Russian economy and financial system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: He built up a pretty impressive team of technocrats from everything, the central bank and the economics and finance ministries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: who really got the country back into shape again and solvent, paid off all of the debts and really started to build the country back up again domestically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And, you know, the first couple of terms, again, putting Chechnya to one side, which was a little hard because, I mean, there was a lot of atrocities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And I have to say that he was pretty involved in all of that because the FSB, which he'd headed previously,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you know, was in charge of wrapping up Chechnya and it created, you know, kind of a very strange sort of system of fealty,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: almost a feudal system in the kind of relationship between Putin at the top and Kadirov in Chechnya.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And there was quite a lot of distortions, you know, kind of as a result of that in the way that the Russian Federation was run,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you know, a lot more of an emphasis on the security services, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But there was a lot of pragmatism, you know, opening up the country for business, you know, basically extending relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I would say that, you know, by the end of those first couple of terms of Putin, Russians were living their best lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You know, there was a lot of opportunity for people. People's labor was being paid for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: They weren't being taxed. The taxes were coming out of the extractive industries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: There was, you know, kind of a sense of much more political pluralism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It wasn't the kind of the chaos of the Eltsin period. And then you see a shift.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And it's pretty much when he comes back into power again in 2011, 2012.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And that's when we see a kind of a different phase emerging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And, you know, part of it is the larger international environment, where Putin himself has become kind of convinced that the United States is out to get him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And part of it goes back to the decision on the part of the United States to invade Iraq in 2003.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: There's also, you know, the recognition of Kosovo in 2008 and, you know, the whole kind of machinations around all kinds of other issues of NATO expansion and elsewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But Iraq in 2003 and this kind of whole idea after that that the United States is in the business of regime change and perhaps, you know, has him in his crosshairs as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But there's also then kind of, I think, a sense of building crisis after the financial crisis and the Great Recession, 2008, 2009,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: because I think Putin up until then believed in the whole idea of the global financial system and that Russia was prospering and that Russia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you know, part of the G8 and actually could be genuinely one of the major economic and financial powers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And then suddenly he realizes that in the West is incompetent, that, you know, we totally mismanaged the economy of our own,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: the financial crash in the United States, the kind of blowing up of the of the housing bubble and that we were feckless and that that had global reverberations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And he's prime minister, of course, you know, in this kind of period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But then, you know, I think that that kind of compels him to kind of come back into the presidency and try to kind of take things under control again in 2007, 2012.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And he also starts to kind of focus on also the domestic environment because his return to the presidency is met by protests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And so after that, we see Putin going on a very different footing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that in that same time frame, I'm going to all these conferences in Russia where Putin is and Peskov, his press secretary, and they talk about him reading Russian history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: but also the collapse of the Russian empire before it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: but he starts to obsess about the past and start to take things in a very different direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: like right-wing nationalist forces. But it's pervasive in the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And it's especially pervasive in the KGB and in the security sector.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: talking about the Cuban missile crisis and secret diplomacy and how we negotiate a way Ukraine in

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: return for Putin not blowing up a nuclear weapon. So he's got a lot of people already talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that. So sorry for the difficult and dark question. It could be for you directly or more like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: do you think we have a plan for this? What happens if he does drop a nuclear weapon? Do you have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: sense that the United States has a good plan? I know we're talking about it. I think we probably

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: have several plans because it depends on what, where, when, how. But don't, and also don't these

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: things happen very quickly? Well, there's also signaling and signs of movement there. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I want to be very, you know, kind of careful about this. But then the thing is, it's also very

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: important that we do this with other nuclear powers. So the other thing that's different

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: from how it might have been in the past, and particularly different from the Cuban missile

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: crisis and the Euro missile crisis, we're not the only nuclear players. China has an emerging nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: arsenal now, less on the strategic side, but building it up, but very much on the intermediate

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: range and tactical. Kim Jong-un is firing off weapons left, right and center at the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: In North Korea, we've got other rogue states. Putin's behaving like a rogue state, just to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: very clear here. And this is what we've got with Kim Jong-un in North Korea. We've also got India

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: and Pakistan. And we've got other states we're not supposed to talk about that we know have

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: nuclear capacities and others that would like to have nuclear capacity. And the whole question here

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: is about also proliferation. Getting back to that time when Ukraine had nuclear weapons, at least

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: there on its territory, in sort of Belarus and Kazakhstan, you've got to wonder, was it wise for

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: them to give it up? We were worried about kind of loose nukes, nuclear weapons, kind of getting out

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of hand proliferation at the time. We wanted fewer nuclear powers. Russia wanted that too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Now we're going to have more. We've got more. And what Putin is saying is, well, that was stupid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: if Ukraine to give up the nuclear weapons. In fact, my colleagues and I back in our report,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: back in the US, kind of suggest they shouldn't give them up. And then that's why we had the

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Budapest memorandum. That's why the United States, the United Kingdom in particular,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: have basically some responsibility and obligation going back to 1994 when they promised Ukraine

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that gave up the nuclear weapons, their territorial integrity and sovereignty would remain intact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: some obligation to actually do something to step up. If we step back from that, this is the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that people are not talking about. What about nuclear proliferation? If you're South Korea,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you're Japan, you're any other country that's kind of worrying about your neighbors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: and what might happen to you? Just like India and Pakistan are both like, whoa,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: we've got to kind of keep our strategic nuclear balance here. Everything is up for question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Saudis will want a nuclear weapon. The Turks already want one. They've talked about one for

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: years. Why should the Iranians be the only one with an Islamic nuclear weapon? And if we know

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that Iran has breakout capacity now, the Saudis and all the other states that are in opposition

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: to Iran will also want to have some nuclear capacity. And the United States before wanted

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: to maintain everything under the nuclear umbrella. One of the reasons why Sweden and Finland are

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: joining NATO is because of suddenly all of these nuclear threats. Sweden was actually the last

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: country on the planet to want to have nuclear weapons. They were actually pushing for a ban

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: on nuclear weapons in the United Nations. Now that Putin's doing the nuclear saber rattling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: they're talking about joining and on the verge of joining a nuclear alliance. See what's happening

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: here. So we have to make it more and more difficult for Putin to even contemplate that. That's why

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: people are saying this is reckless. This is irresponsible. Putin is actually making the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: less safe for himself down the line either, but he's thinking short term here. He's thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: what can I do? What do I actually have? You can also destroy lots of infrastructure as he's doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: You can use subversion. We're worried about all of the undersea cables, all these weird things

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: happening off Orkney or in the Mediterranean or all these other things that are happening,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Nord Stream 2 pipelines, other infrastructure. There's all kinds of other things that he can do

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: as well here. It's not just, again, this is a civilian nuclear threat of blowing up one of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: reactors. Now it's got to be sure about where the wind turns and the wind blows. There's all kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of things to factor in here, but Putin is definitely sitting around calculating with other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: what can I do to turn this around? I mean, he still thinks that he can win this or in other words,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: he can end it on his terms, Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Herson, Zaporizhzhia, and capitulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: all recognized as being part of Russia. Or he can freeze it and then figure out where it goes from

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: there. What other pressure he can put on? I mean, I'm sure he's confident he can get rid of Zelensky

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: and he can prevail over us. I mean, look, the UK is going through prime ministers faster than I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: changing my socks. So it's like he can prevail on the... Basically, he can have an impact on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: political scene in Europe and elsewhere. I mean, again, everyone's talking about winter coming and

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I know Putin's thinking, yeah, great, I've destroyed the infrastructure of Ukraine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Are you worried about the winter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Well, yeah. But I mean, look, the other thing is that we have to start preparing. I mean, we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: to start thinking about this. We've got a wartime economy situation. That's where we are. We've got

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: the home front to think about as well. Putin has declared war on us. He did that on September 30th

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: and he's done it at other points as well. We've just not paid attention. But he was pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: explicit in September 30th. I mean, go back and watch that speech. And he is gambling that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: will go back to basically taking Russian gas and oil, but it's not going to be that simple as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And then the question has to be, do we really think he's going to play fair after that

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: when he's also shown that he can leverage that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It's such a complicated world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It is complicated. It's very complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: And it's never... I mean, it feels like things are heating up. And China is very quiet right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Because they're watching what happens. I mean, for President Xi, he's trying to consolidate his

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: power even further after the party Congress, but he doesn't want to look like he made a mistake by

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: backing Putin. I mean, he thought Putin was also going to be in our... Ukraine would probably be

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: open for massive Chinese investment. China was the largest investor in Ukraine before the war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Largest single investor. I mean, the EU was bigger, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: How do you hope the war ends in Ukraine?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Well, I mean, I do hope it ends with a ceasefire and a negotiated solution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: but it has to be with Russia compromising on something. And that's not where we are right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Do you think both sides might be willing to compromise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Most wars always end in that way. I mean, nobody's ever happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: But they don't seem to... Either side, like legitimately doesn't want to compromise right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Yeah, because the thing is that for Ukraine right now, anything is a compromise at its expense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: right? Vast devastation, unbelievable casualty rates, biggest refugee crisis since World War II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Russia's just said, sorry, this is our territory, it's not just Crimea. I think there could have

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: been a negotiation over that. But Donetsk and Lukánsk, I mean, we've got all kinds of formulas

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: we've had all the way through history of putting things under a kind of guardianship receivership

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of territory, the United Nations, all kinds of different ways of formulating that. We could have

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: easily been creative. But Russia's basically saying, no, sorry, we've taken this. And any

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: other negotiations, just you recognizing this for us not doing more destruction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: That is not the basis for a negotiation. And having people come and just sort of laying

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: those terms down is not a starting position. I think Russia is also in a dilemma of its own

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: making now because Putin has made it very difficult to compromise just by everything that he said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Now, for Ukraine, they've already won a great moral, political and military victory. It's

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: just hard to see it, right? At the particular moment. They've done what the Finns did in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Winter War, which the Finns were devastated by the Winter War as well, but they pushed them back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Now, the Finns lost a lot of territory, they lost Karelia and huge swathes of territory, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: they got to be Finland. And now they're joining NATO, but they've been part of the EU.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: The question is how to get Ukraine to be Ukrainian a success. And that's the challenge. Now, again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: they've already won psychologically, politically, militarily, because Putin hasn't succeeded in what

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: he wanted to do, but he has succeeded in completely and utterly devastating them. And this is the kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of the old Muscovite, the old Russian imperial, old Soviet mentality, going all the way back to

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: when the Muscovites were the bagmen for the Horde, for the Mongols. It was destruction. You don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: play with us, we'll destroy you. People talk about it as mafia, but it's all there. All you have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: go down is you go and see Tarkovsky's Andrey Rublyov. I remember seeing that film when I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: first as a student in Moscow and just being, whoa, this is so brutal. I mean, this is just

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: unremittingly brutal, because the whole point is that you show people who's the boss. The destruction

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: is the point of things as well, because you are emphasizing your domination. And that's what

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Putin is doing right now. He's saying, okay, you want to go in a different direction, so be it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: but I'm going to make you suffer. Remember when Tarkovsky got out of the penal colony,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: when Putin let him out eventually, he said he suffered enough, but he suffered for 10, 11 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I don't think Putin feels that Ukraine has suffered enough at this point, or we have suffered enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: So there's a part of this invasion that's punishment for something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Yeah, it's medieval. I mean, look, we're all capable of the same things, right? There was all

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: that destruction, and that's what Assad was like in Syria, like his father. You destroy because

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you teach him a lesson. And look, Britain did that in the colonial era. I mean, all the history of

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: British colonialism is exactly the same. I mean, all the Mao Mao, you know, and Kenya, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: up until recent times, brutality, teaching people, you know, teaching them a lesson. You have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: suffer. The US did it. I mean, we did it with the Native Americans, you know, we did it all over

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: the place, you know, as well. This is kind of what big states do at different points in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: It's just that, you know, Russia has not moved on from that. And we've learned some lessons late.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: I hope, you know, we fully internalize them of, you know, things that we've done, you know, kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of the past United States, ideally are trying to do better. And most of Europe's trying to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: better as well. Think about France and Algeria, you know, again, you know, we can see this in

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: many different settings. But I think, you know, for Putin right now, he hasn't taught all of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: sufficient a lesson. I just, I talked to hundreds of people in Ukraine and the tough thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: the tough thing, the inspiring thing is that there's a unity. The tough thing is a lot of them speak

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: intensely of hate towards not just Russia, but Russians, Russians. That's how Europeans felt

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: about Germany and Germans at the end of World War II. And generational hate, like, well, I don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: think that hate is going to pass. Well, it might, it might well take a generation. I mean, I, when,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: when I was a kid in the 70s, I went on exchanges to Germany. And that was like, you know, 30 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: more than 30 years after the end of the war, my grandfather who'd fought in World War I,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: wouldn't speak to my parents when they sent me on a, I mean, we hadn't fought in World War II,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: we fought in World War I, he hated the Germans. And he did not want me going, you know, to Germany

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: as an exchange student. He refused to meet, you know, kind of the German kid who, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: came to stay at my house. You know, for example, I mean, it takes a long time to, you know, it

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: takes a long time to get over that. But you do. I mean, and we have, we have in Europe. And that

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: was the whole point of, you know, all of that kind of exercise of European unity after World War II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Now the big challenge is what do we do with Russia? Because a lot of people are talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: we can't have European security without Russia. Other people are saying we can't have a Europe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: you know, kind of with Russia. You know, so how do we deal with this? We've got to basically kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of, it's going to be like Japan and Germany after World War II, after this, just the level

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of the atrocities that have been carried out. As you said, the level of hatred. But we found a way

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: of doing it. Now a lot of it will require change on the part of Russia as well and Russians and

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: really thinking about this. I mean, Gorbachev before tried to do, you know, he was trying to

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: do in the late 1980s with the black spots in, with glasnost, with openness and talking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: Russian history, just kind of never sort of withered on the vine as time went on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: What gives you hope about the future? Well, my hope comes into the fact that we've done things

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335

body.input: before, that we've got ourselves out of tough times and we've overcome stuff and in people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Fiona Hill: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump | Lex Fridman Podcast #335
