body.input: So maybe you can talk about sort of C plus plus has been improving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: There's been a lot of programming language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Do you, where does the arc of history taking us?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Do you hope that there is a unification about the languages with which we communicate in the digital space?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Well, I think that languages should be designed not by clobbering language features together and

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: doing slightly different versions of somebody else's ideas, but through the creation of a set of

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: principles, rules of thumbs, whatever you call them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: I made them for C plus plus and we're trying to teach people in the standards committee about these rules

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: because a lot of people come in and says, I've got a great idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Let's put it in the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: And then you have to ask, why does it fit in the language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Why does it fit in this language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: It may fit in another language and not here, or it may fit here and not the other language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: So you have to work from a set of principles and you have to develop that set of principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: And one example that I sometimes remember is I was sitting down with some of the designers of

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: common Lisp and we were talking about languages and language features and obviously we didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: agree about anything because well, this was not C plus plus and vice versa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: It's too many parentheses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: But suddenly we started making progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: I said, I had this problem and I, I was like, I'm going to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: I said, I had this problem and I developed it according to these ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: And they said, what, why we had that problem, different problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: And we develop it with the same kind of principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: And so we worked through large chunks of C plus plus and large chunks of common Lisp

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: and figured out we actually had similar sets of principles of how to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: But the constraints on our designs were very different and the aims for the usage was very

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: different, but there was commonality in the way you reason about language features and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: fundamental principles you were trying to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: So do you think that's possible to, so they're just like, there is perhaps a unified theory of

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: We've got, what's that 70 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: So each have problems and constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: The others have, but we are very immature compared to physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: So I would look at sort of the philosophical level and look for fundamental principles

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: like you don't leak resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

metadata.title: Podcast: Bjarne Stroustrup: C++ | Lex Fridman Podcast #48

body.input: I'm not sure if you touched that world much, but you could think of programming as a thing

body.input: The following is a conversation with Gwidovan Rasam, creator of Python, one of the most popular

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: programming languages in the world, used in almost any application that involves computers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: from web backend development to psychology, neuroscience, computer vision, robotics, deep

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: learning, natural language processing, and almost any subfield of AI. This conversation is part of

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: MIT course on artificial general intelligence and the artificial intelligence podcast. If you enjoy

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: it, subscribe on YouTube, iTunes, or your podcast provider of choice, or simply connect with me on

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Twitter at Lex Friedman, spelled F-R-I-D. And now here's my conversation with Gwidovan Rasam.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: You were born in the Netherlands in 1956. Your parents and the world around you was

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: deeply impacted by World War II, as was my family from the Soviet Union. So with that context,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: what is your view of human nature? Are some humans inherently good and some inherently evil,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: or do we all have both good and evil within us?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Ouch. I did not expect such a deep one. I guess we all have good and evil potential in us, and a

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: lot of it depends on circumstances and context. Out of that world, at least on the Soviet Union

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: side in Europe, sort of out of suffering, out of challenge, out of that kind of situation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: out of that kind of set of traumatic events, often emerges beautiful art, music, literature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: In an interview I read or heard, you said you enjoyed Dutch literature when you were a child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Can you tell me about the books that had an influence on you in your childhood?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Well, as a teenager, my favorite writer was, my favorite Dutch author was a guy named Willem

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Frederik Hermans, who's writing certainly his early novels were all about sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: ambiguous things that happened during World War II. I think he was a young adult during that time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: and he wrote about it a lot and very interesting, very good books, I thought, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: In a nonfiction way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: No, it was all fiction, but it was very much set in the ambiguous world of resistance against the

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Germans, where often you couldn't tell whether someone was truly in the resistance or really a

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: spy for the Germans. And some of the characters in his novels sort of crossed that line, and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: never really find out what exactly happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And in his novels, there's always a good guy and a bad guy, is the nature of good and evil,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: is it clear there's a hero?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: No, his heroes are often more, his main characters are often anti-heroes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And so they're not very heroic. They're often, they fail at some level to accomplish their lofty goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And looking at the trajectory through the rest of your life, has literature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Dutch or English or translation had an impact outside the technical world that you existed in?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I still read novels. I don't think that it impacts me that much directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Doesn't impact your work. It's just, it's a...

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: It's a separate world. My work is highly technical and sort of the world of art and literature

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: doesn't really directly have any bearing on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: You don't think there's a creative element to the design?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Some would say art, design of a language is art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I'm not disagreeing with that. I'm just saying that sort of I don't feel

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: direct influences from more traditional art on my own creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Right. Of course, you don't feel doesn't mean it's not somehow deeply there in your subconscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Who knows?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Who knows? So let's go back to your early teens, your hobbies

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: were building electronic circuits, building mechanical models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: What, if you can just put yourself back in the mind of that young Guido, 12, 13, 14,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: was that grounded in a desire to create a system? So to create something

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: or was it more just tinkering, just the joy of puzzle solving?

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I think it was more the latter actually. I,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: maybe towards the end of my high school period, I felt confident enough that

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: that I designed my own circuits that were sort of interesting somewhat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: But a lot of that time, I literally just took a model kit and followed the instructions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: putting the things together. I mean, I think the first few years that I built electronics kits,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I really did not have enough understanding of sort of electronics to really understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: what I was doing. I mean, I could debug it and I could sort of follow the instructions very carefully,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: which has always stayed with me. But I had a very naive, very

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: naive model of how a transistor works. And I don't think that in those days,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I had any understanding of coils and capacitors, which actually sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: was a major problem when I started to build more complex digital circuits, because I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: unaware of the sort of the analog part of the how they actually work. And I would have things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: the scheme, the schematic looked, every everything looked fine, and it didn't work. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: what I didn't realize was that there was some megahertz level oscillation that was throwing

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: the circuit off because I had a sort of two wires were too close or the switches were

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: were kind of poorly built. But through that time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I think it's really interesting and destructive to think about because there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: echoes of it are in this time now. So in the 1970s, the personal computer was being born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: So did you sense in tinkering with these circuits, did you sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: the encroaching revolution in personal computing? So if at that point, you're such

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: we'll sit you down and ask you to predict the 80s and the 90s. Do you think you would be able to

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: do so successfully to unroll this, the process that's no, I had no clue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I, I remember, I think in the summer after my senior year, or maybe it was the summer

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: after my junior year. Well, at some point, I think when I was 18, I went on a trip

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: to the math Olympiad in Eastern Europe. And there was like, I was part of the Dutch team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And there were other people who were in the same team. And I think that was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Dutch team. And there were other nerdy kids that sort of had different experiences. And one of them

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: told me about this amazing thing called a computer. And I had never heard that word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: My own explorations in electronics were sort of about very simple digital circuits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And I, I had sort of, I had the idea that I somewhat understood how a digital calculator worked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And so there is maybe some echoes of computers there, but I didn't, didn't, I never made that

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: connection. I didn't know that when my parents were paying for magazine subscriptions using

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: punched cards, that there was something called a computer that was involved at red, those cards

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: and transferred the money between accounts. I was actually also not really interested in those

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: things. It was only when I went to university to study math that I found out that they had a

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: computer and students were allowed to use it. And there was some, you're supposed to talk to

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: that computer by programming it. What would that feel like? Yeah, that was the only thing you could

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: do with it. The computer wasn't really connected to the real world. The only thing you could do was

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: sort of, you typed your program on a bunch of punched cards. You gave the punched cards to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: operator and an hour later, the operator gave you back your printout. And so all you could do was

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: write a program that did something very abstract. And I don't even remember what my first forays

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: into programming were, but they were sort of doing simple math exercises and just to learn how a

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: programming language worked. Did you sense, okay, first year of college, you see this computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: you're able to have a program and it generates some output. Did you start seeing the possibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: of this or was it a continuation of the tinkering with circuits? Did you start to imagine that one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: the personal computer, but did you see it as something that is a tool to get tools like a word

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: processing tool, maybe, maybe for gaming or something, or did you start to imagine that it

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: could be, you know, going to the world of robotics, like you, you know, the Frankenstein picture that

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: you could create an artificial being, there's like another entity in front of you. You did not see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I don't think I really saw it that way. I was really more interested in the tinkering. It's

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: maybe not as sort of a complete coincidence that I ended up sort of creating a programming language

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: which is a tool for other programmers. I've always been very focused on the sort of activity of

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: programming itself and not so much what happens with the program you write. I do remember and I

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: don't remember, maybe in my second or third year, probably my second actually, someone pointed out

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: to me that there was this thing called Conway's Game of Life. You're probably familiar with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I think in the seventies, I think, is when he came up with it. So there was a Scientific American

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: column by someone who did a monthly column about mathematical diversions. I'm also blanking out on

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: the guy's name. It was very famous at the time and I think up to the next year, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I think up to the nineties or so. One of his columns was about Conway's Game of Life. He had

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: some illustrations and he wrote down all the rules. There was the suggestion that this was

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: philosophically interesting, that that was why Conway had called it that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: All I had was the two pages photocopy of that article. I don't even remember where I got it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: but it spoke to me and I remember implementing a version of that game

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: for the batch computer we were using where I had a whole Pascal program that sort of read

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: an initial situation from input and read some numbers that said, do so many generations and

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: print every so many generations and then out would come pages and pages of sort of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Patterns of different kinds. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Yeah. I remember much later, I've done a similar thing using Python, but I'd sort of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: that original version I wrote at the time, I found interesting because I combined it with

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: some trick I had learned during my electronics hobbyist times. I essentially first on paper,

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: I designed a simple circuit built out of logic gates that took nine bits of input, which is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: sort of the cell and its neighbors and produced a new value for that cell. And it's like a combination

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: of a half adder and some other clipping, it's actually a full adder. And so I had worked that

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: out and then I translated that into a series of Boolean operations on Pascal integers where you

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: could use the integers as bitwise values. And so I could basically generate 60 bits

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: of a generation in like eight instructions or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: Nice. So I was proud of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Guido van Rossum: Python | Lex Fridman Podcast #6

body.input: And he even talks about a city as something like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: where everybody, you have your life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but then you have all these alternate lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And every time you make any decision,

body.input: but in this Invisible Cities, there's a little string

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that goes toward that alternate life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And then the city becomes this weaving of all the strings

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of people's real lives and the alternate lives

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that they could have taken had they made

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: any other different steps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So that part, it's like a deep philosophical question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: It's not just for us, it's for all of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: It's baked into evolutionary biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: It's just what are the different strategies

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: for different species to achieve fitness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And there are some of the different corals or other fish

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: where they just kind of release the eggs into the water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And there's all different kinds of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And then you're right in my book, Hacking Darwin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and it's the full title is Hacking Darwin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Genetic Engineering and the Future of Humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: I kind of go deep into exploring

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: the big picture implications

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of the future of human reproduction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: We are already participating in a revolutionary

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: transformation, not just because of the diagnostics

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that we have, things like ultrasound,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but because now an increasing number of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: are being born through in vitro fertilization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: which means the eggs are extracted from the mother,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: they're fertilized by the father's sperm in vitro in a lab,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and then re-implanted in the mother.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: On top of that, there's a somewhat newer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but still now older technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: called pre-implantation genetic testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so as everyone knows from high school biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: you have the fertilized egg,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and then it goes one cell to two cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to four to eight and whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And after around five days in this PGT process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: a few cells are extracted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So let's say you have 10 fertilized eggs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: early stage embryos, a few cells are extracted from each,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and those cells, if they would,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: the ones that are extracted would end up becoming

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: the placenta, but every one of our cells has,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: other than a few, has our full genome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so then you sequence those cells,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and with pre-implantation genetic testing now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: what you can do is you can screen out deadly single gel,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: a single gene mutation disorders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: things that could be deadly or life ruining.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so people use it to determine

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: which of those 10 early stage embryos

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to implant in a mother.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: As we shift towards a much greater understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of genetics, and that is part of our,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: just the broader genetics revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but within that, in our transition from personalized

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to precision healthcare, more and more of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: are going to have our whole genome sequenced,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: because it's gonna be the foundation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of getting personalized healthcare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: We're going to have already millions, but very soon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: billions of people who've had their whole genome sequenced,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and then we'll have big databases

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of people's genetic genotypic information

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and life or phenotypic information,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and using, coming into your area,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: our tools of machine learning and data analytics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we're going to be able to increasingly understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: patterns of genetic expression, even though we're all different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So predict how that genetic information will get expressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Correct, correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Never perfectly, perhaps, but more and more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: always more and more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so with that information, we aren't going to just be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: even now, we aren't going to just be selecting

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: based on which of these 10 early stage embryos

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: is carrying a deadly genetic disorder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but we'll be able to know everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that can be partly or entirely predicted by genetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And there's a lot of our humanity

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that fits into that category.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And certainly, simple traits like height and eye color

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: I mean, height is not at all simple,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but if you have good nutrition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: it's entirely or mostly genetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: But even personality traits and personality styles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: there are a lot of things that we see

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: just as the experience, the beauty of life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that are partly have a genetic foundation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so whatever part of these traits are definable

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and influenced by genetics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we're going to have greater and greater predictability

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: within a range.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so selecting those embryos will be informed

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: by that kind of knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And that's why in Hacking Darwin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: I talk about embryo selection as being a key driver

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of the future of human evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then on top of that, there is in 2012,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Shinya Yamanaka, amazing Japanese scientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: won the Nobel Prize for developing a process

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: for creating what are called

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: induced pluripotent stem cells, IPS cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And what IPS cells are is you can induce an adult cell

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to go back in evolutionary time

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and become a stem cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And a stem cell is like when we're a fertilized egg,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: like our entire blueprint is in that one cell

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and that cell can be anything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but then our cells start to specialize

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and that's why we have skin cells and blood cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and all the different types of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So with the Yamanaka process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we can induce an adult cell to become a stem cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So the relevance to this story is what you can do

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and it works now in animal models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And as far as I know, it hasn't yet been done in humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but it works pretty well in animal models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: You take any adult cell,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but skin cells are probably the easiest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: You induce this skin cell into a stem cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And if you just take a little skin graft,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: it would have millions of cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: You induce those skin cells into stem cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then you induce those stem cells into egg precursor cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then you induce those egg precursor cells into eggs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: egg cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then because we have this massive overabundance

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of male sperm, then you could fertilize,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: let's call it 10,000 of the mother's eggs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So you have 10,000 eggs which are fertilized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Sounds like a party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then you have an automated process

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: for what I mentioned before in pre-implantation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: genetic testing, you grow them all for five days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: You extract a few cells from each.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: You test them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And that's why I had a piece in the New York Times

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: a couple of years ago, imagining what it would be like

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to go to a fertility clinic in the year 2050.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And the choice is not-

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Not humans involved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Well, no, no, there are, but the choice is not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: do you want a kid who does or doesn't have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: let's call it Tay-Sachs?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: It's a whole range of possibilities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but we don't solve the problem of climate change,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: well, kind of who cares?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: We didn't have a pandemic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but we wiped everybody out from climate change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And let's just say, you get where this is going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that we organize ourselves and we solve climate change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And then we have a nuclear war

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: because everybody's, particularly China now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: but US, the former Soviet Union,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: are building all these nuclear weapons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Who cares that we solved climate change

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: because we're all gone anyway

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and the meta category bringing all of those things together

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: was this mismatch between the increasingly global

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and shared nature of the biggest challenges that we face

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and our inability to solve that entire category of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And there's a historical issue,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: which is that prior to the 30 years war in the 17th century,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we had all these different kinds of sovereignty

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and religious and different kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of organizational principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And everybody got in this war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And in this series of treaties

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that together are called the Peace of Westphalia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: the framework for the modern,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: what we now understand as the modern nation state was laid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And then through colonialism and other means,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that idea of a state is what it is today

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: spread throughout the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Then through particularly the late 19th

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and early 20th century,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we realized how unstable that system was

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: because you always had these jockeying

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: between sovereign states and some were rising

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and some were falling and you ended up in war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And that was the genius of the generations

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: who came together in 1945 in San Francisco

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and the planning had even started before then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: who said, well, we can't just have that world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: We need to have an overlay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And we talked about the UN and the WHO

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of systems which transcend our national sovereignty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: They don't get rid of them, but they transcend them

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: so we can solve this category of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: But we're now reaching a point where our reach as humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: even individually, but collectively is so great

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that there's a mismatch between, as I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: the nature of the problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: and the ability to solve those problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And unless we can address

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: that broader global collective action problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: we're going to extinct ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And we see these different, what I call verticals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: whether it's climate change

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: or anything else, but none of those can succeed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And frankly, it doesn't even matter if one succeeds

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: because all of them have the potential

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: to lead to extinction level events.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: So anyways, I gave that talk and that talk went viral.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: of the pandemics wanting to do something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And it's just been this incredible journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: Well, that is, but there's a macro, meta problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: which is the global collective action problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: And so the idea is even if we just focus on the verticals

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: our national leaders and corporate leaders

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

body.input: They're maximizing for national interest,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247

metadata.title: Podcast: Jamie Metzl: Lab Leak Theory | Lex Fridman Podcast #247
