body.input: Can you give advice to people who are undergraduates today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: What does it take to take advice on their journey

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: if they're interested in machine learning, in AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: in the ideas of markets from economics to psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: and all the kinds of things that you're exploring?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: What steps should they take on that journey?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Well, yeah, first of all, the door is open.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And second, it's a journey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I like your language there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It is not that you're so brilliant

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: and you have great, brilliant ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And therefore, that's just how you have success

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: or that's how you enter into the field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It's that you apprentice yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You spend a lot of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You work on hard things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You try and pull back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And you be as broad as you can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You talk to lots of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And it's like entering in any kind of a creative community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: There's years that are needed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And human connections are critical to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I think about being a musician

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: or being an artist or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You don't just immediately, from day one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: you're a genius and therefore you do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: No, you practice really, really hard on basics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And you be humble about where you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And you realize you'll never be an expert on everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So you kind of pick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And there's a lot of randomness and a lot of luck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But luck just kind of picks out which branch of the tree

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: you go down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But you'll go down some branch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So yeah, it's a community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So the graduate school is, I still

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: think, is one of the wonderful phenomena

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: that we have in our world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It's very much about apprenticeship

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: with an advisor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It's very much about a group of people you belong to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It's a four or five year process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So it's plenty of time to start from kind of nothing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: to come up to something, more expertise,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: and then to start to have your own creativity start

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: to flower, even surprising your own self.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And it's a very cooperative endeavor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I think a lot of people think of science as highly competitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I think in some other fields, it might be more so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Here, it's way more cooperative than you might imagine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And people are always teaching each other something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And people are always more than happy to be clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I feel I'm an expert on certain kind of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But I'm very much not expert on lots of other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And a lot of them are relevant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And a lot of them are, I should know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: but should in some sense, you don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I'm always willing to reveal my ignorance to people around me

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: so they can teach me things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I think a lot of us feel that way about our field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So it's very cooperative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I might add it's also very international,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: because it's so cooperative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: We see no barriers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And so the nationalism that you see,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: especially in the current era and everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: is just at odds with the way that most of us think about what we're doing here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: This is a human endeavor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And we cooperate and are very much trying to do it together

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: for the benefit of everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So last question, where and how and why did you learn French?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And which language is more beautiful, English or French?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So first of all, I think Italian is actually more beautiful than French and English.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I also speak that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I'm married to an Italian and I have kids and we speak Italian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Anyway, all kidding aside, every language allows you to express things a bit differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And it is one of the great fun things to do in life, is to explore those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So in fact, when kids or teens or college students ask me what they study,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I say, well, do what your heart is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Certainly do a lot of math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Math is good for everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But do some poetry and do some history and do some language too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Throughout your life, you'll want to be a thinking person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You'll want to have done that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: For me, French I learned when I was, I'd say, a late teen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I was living in the middle of the country in Kansas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And not much was going on in Kansas, with all due respect to Kansas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And so my parents happened to have some French books on the shelf.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And just in my boredom, I pulled them down and I found this is fun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I kind of learned the language by reading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And when I first heard it spoken, I had no idea what was being spoken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But I realized I somehow knew it from some previous life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And so I made the connection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But then I traveled and just I love to go beyond my own barriers and my own comfort or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I found myself on trains in France next to, say, older people who had lived a whole life of their own.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And the ability to communicate with them was special.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And the ability to also see myself in other people's shoes and have empathy and kind of work on that language as part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So after that kind of experience and also embedding myself in French culture, which is quite amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And languages are rich, not just because there's something inherently beautiful about it, but it's all the creativity that went into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I learned a lot of songs, read poems, read books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And then I was here actually at MIT where we're doing the podcast today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And young professor, not yet married and had a lot of friends in the area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I just didn't have a board person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I said I heard a lot of Italians around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: There's happened to be a lot of Italians at MIT, a lot of Italian professors for some reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And so I was kind of vaguely understanding what they're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I said, well, I should learn this language too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And then later met my spouse and Italian became a part of my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But I go to China a lot these days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I go to Asia, I go to Europe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And every time I go, I kind of am amazed by the richness of human experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And people don't have any idea if you haven't traveled kind of how amazingly rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I love the diversity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It's not just a buzzword to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: It really means something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I love to embed myself with other people's experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And so learning language is a big part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I think I've said in some interview at some point that if I had millions of dollars and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: infinite time or whatever, what would you really work on if you really wanted to do AI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And for me, that is natural language and really done right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Deep understanding of language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: That's to me an amazingly interesting scientific challenge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: One we're very far away on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: One we're very far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But good natural language people are kind of really invested in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I think a lot of them see that's where the core of AI is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: That if you understand that, you really help human communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You understand something about the human mind, the semantics that come out of the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And I agree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I think that will be such a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: So I didn't do that in my career just because I kind of I was behind in the early days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I didn't kind of know enough of that stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I was at MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I didn't learn much language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: And it was too late at some point to kind of spend a whole career doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: But I admire that field and so in my little way by learning language, you know, kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: that part of my brain has been trained up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: Jan was right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: You truly are the Miles Davis of machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael I. Jordan: Machine Learning, Recommender Systems, and Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #74

body.input: I don't think this is a better place than it is.

body.input: Merci beaucoup.

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Daleep George. Do you think we need to understand the brain in

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: order to build it? Yes. If you want to build the brain, we definitely need to understand how it

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: works. So Blue Brain or Henry Markram's project is trying to build a brain without understanding it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: just trying to put details of the brain from neuroscience experiments into a giant simulation

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: by putting more and more neurons, more and more details. But that is not going to work because

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: when it doesn't perform as what you expect it to do, then what do you do? You just keep adding more

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: details. How do you debug it? So unless you understand, unless you have a theory about

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: how the system is supposed to work, how the pieces are supposed to fit together, what they're going

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: to contribute, you can't build it. At the functional level, understand. So can you actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: linger on and describe the Blue Brain project? It's kind of a fascinating principle and idea

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: to try to simulate the brain. We're talking about the human brain, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Right. Human brains and rat brains or cat brains have lots in common that the cortex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the neocortex structure is very similar. So initially they were trying to just simulate

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: a cat brain. To understand the nature of evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: To understand the nature of evil. Or as it happens in most of these simulations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: you easily get one thing out, which is oscillations. Yeah, if you simulate a large

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: number of neurons, they oscillate. And you can adjust the parameters and say that, oh,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: oscillations match the rhythm that we see in the brain, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Oh, I see. So the idea is, is the simulation at the level of individual neurons?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Yeah. So the Blue Brain project, the original idea as proposed was, you put very detailed

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: biophysical models of neurons and you interconnect them according to the statistics of connections

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: that we have found from real neuroscience experiments. And then turn it on and see what

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: happens. And these neural models are incredibly complicated in themselves, right? Because these

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: neurons are modeled using this idea called Hodgkin-Huxley models, which are about how

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: signals propagate in a cable. And there are active dendrites, all those phenomena,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: which those phenomena themselves, we don't understand that well. And then we put in

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: connectivity, which is part guesswork, part observed. And of course, if you do not have any

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: theory about how it is supposed to work, we just have to take whatever comes out of it as, okay,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: this is something interesting. But in your sense, like these models of the way signal travels

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: along, like with the axons and all the basic models, they're too crude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Oh, well, actually, they are pretty detailed and pretty sophisticated. And they do replicate

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the neural dynamics. If you take a single neuron and you try to turn on the different channels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the calcium channels and the different receptors, and see what the effect of turning off those

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: channels are in the neurons spike output, people have built pretty sophisticated models of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And they are, I would say, in the regime of correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Well, see, the correctness, that's interesting, because you mentioned it at several levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: The correctness is measured by looking at some kind of aggregate statistics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: It would be more the spiking dynamics of a single neuron.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Spiking dynamics of a single neuron, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And yeah, these models, because they are going to the level of mechanism, right? So they are

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: basically looking at, okay, what is the effect of turning on an ion channel? And you can model that

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: using electric circuits. So it is not just a function fitting. People are looking at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: mechanism underlying it and putting that in terms of electric circuit theory, signal propagation

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: theory, and modeling that. And so those models are sophisticated, but getting a single neuron

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: model 99% right does not still tell you how to... It would be the analog of getting a transistor

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: model right and now trying to build a microprocessor. And if you did not understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: how a microprocessor works, but you say, oh, I now can model one transistor well, and now I will just

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: try to interconnect the transistors according to whatever I could guess from the experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: and try to simulate it, then it is very unlikely that you will produce a functioning microprocessor.

body.input: When you want to produce a functioning microprocessor, you want to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: maybe you are familiar with it, that I remember going through in a reading group that approaches

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: a microprocessor from a perspective of a neuroscientist. I think it basically uses all the tools that we have of neuroscience to try to understand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: like as if we just aliens showed up to study computers and to see if those tools could be used to get any kind of sense of how the microprocessor works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: I think the final takeaway from at least this initial exploration is that we are screwed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: There is no way that the tools of neuroscience would be able to get us to anything, like not even Boolean logic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: I mean, it is just any aspect of the architecture of the function of the processes involved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the clocks, the timing, all that, you can't figure that out from the tools of neuroscience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Yes, I am very familiar with this particular paper. I think it was called,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Can a Neuroscientist Understand a Microprocessor? Something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Following the methodology in that paper, even an electrical engineer would not understand microprocessors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: I don't think it is that bad in the sense of saying, neuroscientists do find valuable things by observing the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: They do find good insights, but those insights cannot be put together just as a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: You have to investigate what are the computational underpinnings of those findings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: How do all of them fit together from an information processing perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, I don't want to have all of these neuroscientists saying, oh, they are not finding anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: No, that paper almost went to that level of neuroscientists will never understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: That's not true. I think they do find lots of useful things, but it has to be put together in a computational framework.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: The AI systems will be listening to this podcast a hundred years from now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: There is some non-zero probability they will find your words laughable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: I remember humans thought they understood something about the brain that are totally clueless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: There is a sense about neuroscience that we may be in the very early days of understanding the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: But, I mean, that's one perspective. In your perspective, how far are we into understanding any aspect of the brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Well, and on that point, one of the Wright brothers, I think two years before, said that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Even during their experimentation. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: I mean, that's a tribute to when... That's like the entrepreneurial battle of depression,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Even the person that's in it is not able to see, estimate correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Exactly. But I can tell from the point of objectively what are the things that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: know about the brain and how that can be used to build AI models, which can then go back and

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: inform how the brain works. So, my way of understanding the brain would be to basically say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: look at the insights neuroscientists have found, understand that from a computational angle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: information processing angle, build models using that. And then building that model,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: which is a functional model, which is doing the task that we want the model to do. It is not just

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: trying to model a phenomena in the brain. It is trying to do what the brain is trying to do on

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the whole functional level. And building that model will help you fill in the missing pieces

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: that biology just gives you the hints. And building the model fills in the rest of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: pieces of the puzzle. And then you can go and connect that back to biology and say, okay, now

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: it makes sense that this part of the brain is doing this, or this layer in the cortical circuit

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: is doing this. And then continue this iteratively, because now that will inform new experiments in

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: neuroscience. And of course, building the model and verifying that in the real world will also

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: tell you more about does the model actually work? And you can refine the model, find better ways of

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: putting these neuroscience insights together. So, I would say it is... Neuroscientists alone,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: just from experimentation, will not be able to build a functional model of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, there's lots of efforts, which are very impressive efforts in collecting more and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: connectivity data from the brain. How are the microcircuits of the brain connected with each

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: other? Those are beautiful, by the way. Those are beautiful. And at the same time, those do not

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: itself, by themselves, convey the story of how does it work? And somebody has to understand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: okay, why are they connected like that? And what are those things doing? And we do that by building

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: models in AI, using hints from neuroscience, and repeat the cycle. So, what aspect of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: are useful in this whole endeavor? Which, by the way, I should say, you're both a neuroscientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: and an AI person. I guess the dream is to both understand the brain and to build AGI systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, it's like an engineer's perspective of trying to understand the brain. So, what aspects of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: brain functionally speaking, like you said, do you find interesting? Yeah, quite a lot of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: All right. So, one is, if you look at the visual cortex, and the visual cortex is a large part of

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the brain, I forget the exact fraction, but a huge part of our brain area is occupied by just vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, visual cortex is not just a feed-forward cascade of neurons. There are a lot more feedback

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: connections in the brain compared to the feed-forward connections. And it is surprising

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: to the level of detail neuroscientists have actually studied this. If you go into neuroscience

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: literature and poke around and ask, have they studied what will be the effect of poking a neuron

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: in level IT in level V1? And have they studied that? And you will say, yes, they have studied that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, every possible combination. I mean, it's not a random exploration at all. It's very

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: hypothesis-driven. Experimental neuroscientists are very, very systematic in how they probe the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: brain because experiments are very costly to conduct. They take a lot of preparation. They

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: need a lot of control. So, they are very hypothesis-driven in how they probe the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And often what I find is that when we have a question in AI about, has anybody probed how

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: lateral connections in the brain works? And when you go and read the literature, yes, people have

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: probed it and people have probed it very systematically. And they have hypotheses about

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: how those lateral connections are supposedly contributing to visual processing. But of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: they haven't built very, very functional detailed models of it. By the way, how do the studies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: sorry to interrupt, do they stimulate like a neuron in one particular area of the visual cortex

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: and then see how the signal travels kind of thing? Very, very fascinating experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, I can give you one example I was impressed with. So, before going to that, let me give you

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: overview of how the layers in the cortex are organized. Visual cortex is organized into

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: roughly four hierarchical levels. So, V1, V2, V4, IT. And in V1- What happened to V3?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Well, yeah, there's another pathway. Okay. So, I'm talking about just object recognition pathway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: All right, cool. And then in V1 itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: there is a very detailed micro circuit in V1 itself. There is organization within a level

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: itself. The cortical sheet is organized into multiple layers and there are columnar structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And this layer-wise and columnar structure is repeated in V1, V2, V4, IT, all of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And the connections between these layers within a level, in V1 itself, there are six layers roughly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: and the connections between them, there is a particular structure to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And now, so one example of an experiment people did is when you present a stimulus, which is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: let's say, requires separating the foreground from the background of an object. So, it's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: textured triangle on a textured background. And you can check, does the surface settle first,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: or does the contour settle first? Settle?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Settle in the sense that when you finally form the percept of the triangle, you understand where the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: contours of the triangle are, and you also know where the inside of the triangle is, right? That's

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: when you form the final percept. Now, you can ask, what is the dynamics of forming that final percept?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Do the neurons first find the edges and converge on where the edges are, and then they find the

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: inner surfaces, or does it go the other way around? The other way around. So, what's the answer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: In this case, it turns out that it first settles on the edges, it converges on the edge hypothesis

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: first, and then the surfaces are filled in from the edges to the inside. That's fantastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And the detail to which you can study this, it's amazing that you can actually not only find

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the temporal dynamics of when this happens, and then you can also find which layer in V1,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: which layer is encoding the edges, which layer is encoding the surfaces, and which layer is encoding

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the feedback, which layer is encoding the feedforward, and what's the combination of

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: them that produces the final person. And these kinds of experiments stand out when you try to

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: explain illusions. One example of a favorite illusion of mine is the Kinesa triangle. I don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: know that you are familiar with this one. So, this is an example where it's a triangle, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: only the corners of the triangle are shown in the stimulus. So, they look like kind of Pac-Man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Oh, the black Pac-Man. Yeah. And then you start to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Your visual system hallucinates the edges. And when you look at it, you will see a faint edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And you can go inside the brain and look, do actually neurons signal the presence of this edge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And if they signal, how do they do it? Because they are not receiving anything from the input.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: The input is black for those neurons. So, how do they signal it? When does the signaling happen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, if a real contour is present in the input, then the neurons immediately signal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: oh, okay, there is an edge here. When it is an illusory edge, it is clearly not in the input.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: It is coming from the context. So, those neurons fire later. And you can say that, okay,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: it's the feedback connections that is causing them to fire. And they happen later. And you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: find the dynamics of them. So, these studies are pretty impressive and very detailed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, by the way, just to step back, you said that there may be more feedback connections

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: than feedforward connections. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: First of all, just for like a machine learning folks, I mean, that's crazy that there's all

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: these feedback connections. We often think about, thanks to deep learning, you start to think about

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the human brain as a kind of feedforward mechanism. So, what the heck are these

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: feedback connections? Yeah. What's the dynamics? What are we supposed to think about them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Yeah. So, this fits into a very beautiful picture about how the brain works. So,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the beautiful picture of how the brain works is that our brain is building a model of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, our visual system is building a model of how objects behave in the world. And we are

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: constantly projecting that model back onto the world. So, what we are seeing is not just a

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: feedforward thing that just gets interpreted in a feedforward part. We are constantly projecting

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: our expectations onto the world. And what the final percept is a combination of what we project

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: onto the world combined with what the actual sensory input is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Almost like trying to calculate the difference and then trying to interpret the difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Yeah. I wouldn't put it as calculating the difference. It's more like what is the best

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: explanation for the input stimulus based on the model of the world I have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Got it. Got it. And that's where all the illusions come in. But that's an incredibly efficient

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: process. So, the feedback mechanism, it just helps you constantly, yeah. So, hallucinate how

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: the world should be based on your world model and then just looking at if there's novelty,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: like trying to explain it. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Hence, that's why movement, we detect movement really well. There's all these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: And this is like at all different levels of the cortex you're saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Every. This happens at the lowest level,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: at the highest level. Exactly. Yes. Yeah. In fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: feedback connections are more prevalent everywhere in the cortex. And so, one way to think about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: and there's a lot of evidence for this, is inference. So, basically, if you have a model

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: of the world and when some evidence comes in, what you are doing is inference. You are trying to now

body.input: explain this evidence using your model of the world. And this inference includes projecting

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: your model onto the evidence and taking the evidence back into the model and doing an

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: iterative procedure. And this iterative procedure is what happens using the feed-forward feedback

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: propagation. And examples are everywhere. We see these kinds of things everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, you have competing models of the world that try to explain. What do you mean by explain away?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: Yeah. So, neural networks are one class of machine learning models. You have a distributed set of

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: nodes which are called the neurons. Each one is doing a dot product and you can approximate

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: any function using this multi-level network of neurons. So, that's a class of models which are

body.input: useful for function approximation. There is another class of models in machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: called probabilistic graphical models. And you can think of them as each node in that

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: model is variable, which is talking about something. It can be a variable representing

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: representing is there an object present in the world or not. And then, so it is another way of

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: encoding knowledge. And then, once you encode the knowledge, you can do inference in the right way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: What is the best way to explain some set of evidence using this model that you encoded?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

body.input: So, when you encode the model, you are encoding the relationship between these different variables.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115

metadata.title: Podcast: Dileep George: Brain-Inspired AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #115
