metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: Yes, and it got worse and I heard a pop. I don't know what it was, but I know it really hurt. So I

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: came back standing up and there's a famous video that goes on the internet about when I go back in

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: in terms of wrestling? So he's an exceptionally difficult opponent to take down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: Yeah. Well, at first I knew I had a good jab, to stay always from the outside, fight him from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: outside and use my footwork because he was like a tank. He was much bigger and much stronger than me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: I never wanted to stay in front of him. So he was all the way out or all the way in. And when I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: coming all the way in, it was with my proactive or reactive takedown where I myself initiated

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: the takedown by using a distraction like a jab to make his end goes up. And then I go with a single

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: or double leg or to react, baiting him for him to come hit me. And then while he's coming to hit me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: I go change level and that's the way I like to take my opponent down. Some guys, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: like Cabe, for example, he's very good at bringing his opponent to defense and use chain wrestling to

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: take his opponent down. I find that for me, for myself, I specialize more into explosive takedown

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: in the center of the octagon because I found it more economical for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: What did you see? You were commenting, John, about the wrestling. That was quite interesting. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Georges St-Pierre, John Danaher & Gordon Ryan: The Greatest of All Time | Lex Fridman Podcast #260

body.input: also, can you generally comment on the fact that George St. Pierre, who don't, I don't think you

body.input: Thirdly, I would say if you want to become something truly impressive in life,

body.input: about how things work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So one of the limits of computer performance

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: is branch prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So, and there's a whole bunch of ideas

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: about how good you could predict a branch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And people said, there's a limit to it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: it's an asymptotic curve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and somebody came up with a better way

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: to do branch prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It was a lot better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And he published a paper on it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and every computer in the world now uses it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And it was one idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So the engineers who build branch prediction hardware

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: were happy to drop the one kind of training array

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and put it in another one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So it was a real idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And branch prediction is one of the key problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: underlying all of sort of the lowest level of software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It boils down to branch prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Boils down to uncertainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: Computers are limited by,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: single thread computers are limited by two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: The predictability of the path of the branches

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: and the predictability of locality of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So we have predictors that now predict

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: both of those pretty well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So memories, a couple hundred cycles away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: local cache is a couple cycles away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: When you're executing fast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: virtually all the data has to be in the local cache.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: So a simple program says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: add one to every element and array.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: It's kind of random.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And you can think that's really unpredictable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: And then you make this big predictor

metadata.title: Podcast: Jim Keller: The Future of Computing, AI, Life, and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #162

body.input: that looks at this kind of pattern and you realize,
